utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 473, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We spoke earlier about Petrinja. Could we look now at 65 ter Exhibit 2452, please? What is this document entitled, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The document has been titled as follows, "Basic concepts of works acknowledge activities for the Petrinja municipality steering committee for the establishment of the Serbian democratic party for the Serb lands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a stirring committee or a steering committee? What does it stir?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I assume that that's a typo and it's supposed to be steering committee, Your Honour, but it might -- maybe it was stirring something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could scroll down, please, on this page, what is the date of the document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The date of this document is February 19, 94.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we look at the next page, please? Now if we could look at the next page -- finish scrolling down and then turn to the next page, please? Are you able to tell us what this document is, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This document basically tells about the establishment of the steering committee for this particular Serbian Democratic Party of Serb lands in Petrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we look at the next page, please? And what is this page about?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: As this page is titled, it's a history of the Serbian Democratic Parties and their situation today at this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we scroll down to the bottom of the page? Can you read that last paragraph for us? There is on page 4. It's on page 4 of both the English and the B/C/S. If you could just read that last paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The last paragraph on this page states as follows: "A state of war was declared on the 17th August 1990 [indiscernible] and it was in this period that an organised armed struggle of the Serb people ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kerkkanen. If you could just read a little bit more slowly because the court reporter will have difficulty keeping up.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: And the paragraph continues: "The first armed forces of Krajina were set up by the current president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Milan Martic. The war still goes on and with the same goal, that of liberating and separating from Croatia and creating a unified state, greater Serbia." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This document was also obtained from the Croatian state archive and its archival storage in Petrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence and given a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have an objection to my friend's moving that it be admitted into evidence, because from the document, one cannot see who authored the document, when or where. There is no reference number, there is no stamp, there is no signature. There is nothing on the document to that effect. Such a document can be drafted by anyone. The only thing the witness sitting here did was to read out parts of the text. Another thing, Your Honour, there are no minutes from this meeting. There are no minutes in handwritten or typewritten form. It does not state who took the minutes or where the meeting was held. The text as it stands is quite arbitrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may the document it's incorrect to say that it's -- that there is no reference to date because there is a reference to a date. And secondly, I think the Trial Chamber has held certainly in its rulings and I believe this is even this may even be addressed in its guidelines for admission of evidence that such things as a stamp or a signature are not requirements for admission into evidence. Third, the witness -- this document just doesn't come out of no where. The witness has testified where the document came from. It came from the archive, and he explained earlier that this is a document that he himself selected from that archive and how documents came to be in the archive. So I think with respect that the objections raised by counsel, Defence counsel, go to weight but should not bar the admission into evidence of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you referred also to the fact that there are no minutes. It doesn't seem to have taken place in a meeting which could contain minutes. It's just a working paper, a basic concept of work and activities for the Petrinja municipality steering committee for the establishment of the Serbian Democratic Party of the Serb lands. I'm not sure why you say that there should be minutes accompanying this document, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to make myself fully clear, after the cover page where it says the steering company for the establishment of this party and where it reads Petrinja municipality, February 1994, there are the contents of the document, where the steering committee's establishment is being moved, as well as its prospective members and then it goes on to items 2, 3, and 4. After that, there is the typewritten text of an introduction, an introductory speech. Someone is addressing citizens, honourable citizens, brothers and sisters and so on. And then the subsequent text is the one that the Prosecutor was referring to. One can absolutely not see who the author of the text is, because the text does propose that some persons become members of the steering committee but it's a proposal. You could have included my own name there as a proposal to be part of the committee. I see this document now for the first time. What I wanted to point out was that such a document could in fact be an absolute manipulation. There is not a single fact on the basis of which we could establish that this is indeed a genuine political initiative launched by someone. This is the difficulty that this document in our submission poses. Another matter which is quite interesting, the document was written in the Latin script. At the time the Krajina used the Cyrillic script as its customary script. That was normally used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I do not understand why you say this is a proposal. Why do you say so?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was merely reading the text before me. The title of the document is basic concept of work and activities of the steering committee. The contents or rather the following page reads, "The establishment of the steering committee in the following composition," and then the text flows on. So this is something that is only about to materialise itself, if this is indeed an initiative, and what also needs to be said is that this is a document originating from the Croatian state archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Milovancevic, I'd like to pose a question to you. What is the inference to be drawn from the fact that the document was written in Latin script whereas the Krajina at the time used Cyrillic script as its customary script?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one cannot exclude a single possibility or a possibility that this may be -- may have been the case. However, all those who were involved in the public life of the Krajina used the typewriters that had the Cyrillic script, whereas Latin script was used by the official Croatian authorities. This in itself does not necessarily have to mean anything, but this -- these are aspects that give rise to doubt, whereas on the other side, there is nothing that would induce us, the Defence, to really arrive at the conclusion that this in fact was a political initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Whiting, is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Recognises, I'll try to address the points raised by Defence council but I think over all again they all go to weight and not to admissibility. I would say, however, that while we do not necessarily know the specific author of this document, we do know from the document that it's a member of the Serbian Democratic Party of the Serb lands. And I think that the document can be evaluated in terms of its authenticity with respect to the -- what's in the document and the context, what it refers to, which I would submit refer to other things that are in evidence in this case. With respect to the final point, that the document is not in -- that's in it's Latin script and not in Cyrillic, we have earlier today admitted a document from Milan Martic himself, it's 65 ter Exhibit 2080 and I don't know what the exhibit number is but it's one of the ones I've gone through and it is in Latin script, it's typed in Latin script, it's not typed in the Cyrillic script, and all the other -- nearly all the other documents that we have admitted -- I'm just flipping through my bundle here, nearly all of them are in Latin-typed script. There may be one in here that's in Cyrillic but I haven't found it yet. So I think that objection is plainly unfounded. But again I think these all go to weight and can be argued by Defence counsel when the Trial Chamber has to consider this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, is it therefore your position that the points you have raised, that the document is in Latin script and not in Cyrillic script and the other points you raised be considered when considering the weight of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this has nothing to do with the probational value of the document, but with elements which serve to show the authenticity of a document. Since this is a document which speaks of a political initiative, then one would expect to have -- to expect to have members of the steering committee signing the document or at least is someone signing the document, but we don't have that, which means that such a document could have been drafted by anyone. Your Honour, this seems to us to be a pamphlet of a sort. That's how the document transpires to us. In order to assess its authenticity, we need to have some elements that would serve as a foundation for either conclusion but we have none of that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You say yourself, Mr. Milovancevic, as you start your last argument that this has nothing to do with probative value of the document but with the elements which serve to show the authenticity of the document. So that -- and as I understand the guidelines are that the Trial Chamber shall admit into evidence any document that has probative value, which is exactly what you are not addressing. You are addressing authenticity, which to my understanding, I think are issues to be addressed when looking at the weight to be attached to the document. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, what is at the centre of the matter is the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well, then. In that event, based on the guidelines, the document will be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number and the authenticity of the document will be looked at when the weight to be attached to the document is considered. Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think it needs to be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 474, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kerkkanen, I want to draw your attention to section 2 of part 3 of your report, which in the English begins on page 49. Does this section talk about the relationship between forces in the RSK and Serb forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And turning to page 55, in the English, which is -- it's the last paragraph of this section, does it state that Martic maintained contacts with both RS police and army of the Republika Srpska VRS?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I state here in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter Exhibit 1448, please? What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The date of this document is the 5th of September 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could just scroll down, now just scroll back up, please. There. Could you tell us what this document is about, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This document is a request from the Main Staff of Bosnian Serb army, and Ratko Mladic, to President of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, RSK, Mr. Milan Martic, for the loan of 15 Orkan rockets for the needs of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The OTP has obtained this document from the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence and given a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 475, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen could we look at page 8 of your report, please, and do you talk there about the beginning of the armed conflict in the SAO Krajina in August of 1990?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on pages 9 and 10 of your report, do you talk about assistance that the SAO Krajina received from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we look, please, at 65 ter Exhibit 1494? Mr. Kerkkanen, do you know what this document is?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This document is a translation of Borisav Jovic's book, the last days of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who is Borisav Jovic, and in particular, do you know who he was at that time, during the year 1990-91?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic was the president of the Presidency of the SFRY Presidency at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was this book published and is it publicly available?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This book has been published and it's available.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go to page 159 of the English and page 177 of the B/C/S, and if it's of assistance, I can also provide the ERN numbers of the pages. And if we could scroll down to the bottom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 159 and what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: This is page 159 in the English. On the B/C/S version, it's page 177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What's the date at the bottom there, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The date on the bottom is the 17th of August 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On the English could we go to page 160? On the B/C/S it's still 177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, I didn't see the date of the 17th August 1990 at page 159. And my -- am I missing something?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, it's on -- no. Or yes. Hang on one second. If we could go back one page previously, could we go back to -- I think you're on 160. Could we go back to 159, please? And let's go to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm obviously on the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honour looks at the court monitor it should be correct on that page, on the court monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see it on the Court monitor. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the way, does this book take the form of a published diary?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. Basically in a sense this book is a diary of events from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go to the next page, please, on the English, to 160? Could you tell us what this entry is about for the 17th of August 1990?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Basically for this particular date, Mr. Jovic writes that there has been an uprising of Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we look now, please, at page 283 in the English and it's page 316 on the B/C/S. And if we could scroll down for the entry of 5 April, 1991, that's the one I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, could you just take a moment to read that entry and tell us what it's about? And I think we'll have to scroll down a little bit. That's fine. Could you tell us what this entry is about, for the 5th of April 1991?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Basically it's a summary from the meeting that Mr. Jovic had with Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, Arijevic [phoen] and Adzic concerning the police in Croatia. Basically the middle paragraph states they will take the following course of action in the -- if the Croats attack them they will take armed action, meaning that they are prepared to use military means in this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you see the sentence that begins, "it is clear that acceptance of the position, that the military" --

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you just read that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The sentence states as follows: "It is clear that the acceptance of the position, the military cannot use weapons. Would be catastrophic for the Serb nation in Croatia. The MUP, which has not armed itself but is instead counting on protection by the JNA, while Croatia has armed its own pro-Ustasha secessionists units." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Finally could we look at page 358 in the English and page 401 in the B/C/S, the entry for the 25th of October 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Oh, I see the time, Your Honour. If I could just finish with this, it will just take another minute. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, could you tell us what this entry is about?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Well, in the beginning of this entry, it's clear that there has been a dispute between let's say political and military leadership about the policy they are having and then further down, Slobodan must be referring to Mr. Milosevic, responds about the actions they have taken, that they have helped them, meaning the Serbs in Croatia, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, are you saying Slobodan is referring to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is there a Slobodan by another surname? Could you give us the surname of that Slobodan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this context, I can't think about anyone else than Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So he's referring to his own -- he's referring to himself? Slobodan refers to Mr. Milosevic? Oh, Jovic. Sorry, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I continue. And then basically Jovic is telling what took place, what happened in this meeting and what Slobodan, meaning Slobodan Milosevic, was responding, they will -- they have helped the Serbs in Croatia apparently and they will continue to do so until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move this document into evidence and ask that it be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 476, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is that now a convenient time, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is, and I apologise for going over, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No problem. Thank you very much. The Court will adjourn and reconvene at quarter to six. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now I'm just going to show three brief video clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before I show the first one we've already noted, Mr. Kerkkanen, in your report, earlier in your testimony, where you talk about assistance from Serbia to the SAO Krajina. The first video clip is 65 ter Exhibit 657 which is V 0002220. Before we play the clip, could you tell us what the source of this video clip is, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This video clip has been obtained from Natasa Kandic who is head of humanitarian law centre in Belgrade, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in order to play the clip I think we need to switch over to the Sanction from the AV booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, whilst we are waiting, could I find out what Sanction is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I may answer that. Sanction is just the computer software programme that plays -- allows us to play the videos in court. It's just a software programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It seems to be on the screen now in computer evidence. If we could play that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, could you tell us what that clip is about, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This clip is an interview of secretary Milan Martic. There was a subtitle telling that he's secretary of SAO Krajina MUP, in the very eastern part of Croatia, in the vicinity of Borovo Selo and Bilje. There were captured with the help of his units or troops and a number of Croats were detained in this action and one of these detainees was interviewed in the end of this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You made a reference to the caption on the screen, and if we could just look at the clip again, I had intended to pause it on that caption but I forgot to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could pause it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that the caption that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Exactly. It reads, as follows, "Milan Martic, secretary of Ministry of the internal affairs of autonomous region of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, during the clip, there is an a reference to the liberation of Bilje. Do you know the date that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The liberation of Bilje took place or the so-called liberation of Bilje took place on the 4th of September 1991. So this clip must be either from that date or the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this clip be admitted into evidence and given a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 477, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, we also talked earlier in your testimony about how in your report you talk about the beginning of the armed conflict in the SAO Krajina and Martic's role in it. And we are going to look at a second clip which is 65 ter Exhibit 665, it's ERN number V 0002250.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now -- before we play this clip I have just a word of explanation about this clip. It's a rather lengthy clip. I think it's about ten minutes long. And the first part of the -- the part that we are particularly interested in is the end of the clip and that's the part that we have the translation for and the translation will play for. However, the beginning part of the clip is included without a translation in order to give context and give a sense of the time that this occurred. And we will -- we can at a later time provide a translation for the first part of the clip. We don't have that available today, I'm afraid. There are, in that first part of the clip that's not translated, you'll see there is a kind of press conference with Milan Babic and in fact many of the answers are translated into English during the press conference so there is to some degree a translation. But as I said it's just in order to give context that I play that part so I just ask the Court to be patient, sit through it, we won't understand all of it but at a certain point the transcript will start rolling and that's the part where the transcript applies to at the end of the clip. If we could play that clip now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "I also would like to say that particularly [indiscernible] that we were recommended that we would be persuaded to accept what the European Community is offering to us regarding our future status. "In SAO Krajina, there is no political dissension. "But in my view, we have the influence of some who have not participated in the actions in the Krajina and who are not represented in the authorities for [indiscernible]. "Let me just to mention the League of Communists' movement against Yugoslavia. "You are probably aware of some other interests and some other influences on Krajina from outside Krajina. "They are present and evident in various ways and particularly through activities of some individuals. "You mentioned Captain Dragan [indiscernible]. I don't know his first name and family name. "And who was engaged by minister Martic [indiscernible]"

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, what was that -- could you tell us what that clip was about, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Very shortly, in the beginning, as it was obvious, there was this press conference in Belgrade, and the second part of this clip was an interview of Mr. Martic, and basically, this interview was about internal conflict in the leadership of SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the source of the clip?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This clip has also -- has been also obtained from Natasa Kandic in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the date of this clip? As best as you can tell.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The first part of this clip makes it clear that it took place soon after the peace conference in The Hague in October or -- no, I can't recall exactly whether it took place in October or November but October or November in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And are there references in the clip to SAO Krajina, are there references to Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Certainly, there are many references to SAO Krajina. Now, I do not recall any other references.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this clip be admitted into evidence and be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 478, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We also talked earlier in your report about -- earlier in your testimony about how your report talks about Captain Dragan and also on pages 25 and 26 of your report, there is -- you talk about Milan Babic. If we could look at the third clip which is 65 ter Exhibit 642, it's V 0003109.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that clip, can I ask a question? You've referred to pages 25 and 26, and I see there are certain deletions on page 25 and page 26. What are we to make of those deletions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, those were the deletions that were ordered by the Court in its order of 28 April 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, what was that clip about?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: The first part of this clip was an interview of Milan Martic, about the conflict between him and Milan Babic, and the second part of this clip is an interview of Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The interview with Captain Dragan, can you tell where that -- where that takes place? Where is that location? Are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: It's very obvious from the image that this interview is taken place either in the fortress of Knin or near the fortress in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Have you yourself been to the fortress in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell what the date of the clip is?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. In his interview Captain Dragan refers to the fact that they were sent away or expelled from SAO Krajina five months earlier, and they were sent away in the autumn of 1991 so this clip must therefore be from the first part of 1992, most likely February or the beginning of March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the source of the clip?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: This clip has been obtained from the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be admitted into evidence and receive a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 479, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic, could we deal with housekeeping matters before you cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber recalls that the Prosecution -- recalls the Prosecution of notice of submission of previously admitted Rule 92 bis evidence. In it mention is made of a new motion vis-a-vis witnesses MM-024 and MM-032. MM-024 motion has been received. What the Chamber would like to know is what is the position with MM-032.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could get back to the Court on that tomorrow, I can't answer that question as I sit here. I'm just not sure. I just don't have track of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, if you can just make a note of that. Look at Prosecution's notice dated the 17th of March 2006 in relation to that -- those two witnesses. Then yesterday, the Chamber raised some issue concerning Witness MM-808, and -- 080, I beg your pardon. What day say? Okay. 080. Are we able to get a response to that motion, Mr. Milovancevic? There is a bit of urgency around those two issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have filed the response, Your Honour, today. We submitted it to the Registry. We took it upon ourselves yesterday to file it today, and we have indeed done so prior to the start of today's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. The Chamber has not been made aware of it. Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can confirm just that we've received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We haven't received it yet. Thank you very much. I will track it down. Those are all the housekeeping issues that we wanted to raise. Mr. Milovancevic, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, my name is Predrag Milovancevic, attorney at law, Defence counsel for Mr. Martic. We will start now with your cross-examination, which is something you are surely familiar with. I will put questions to you which the Defence deems relevant and important. In order to ensure that the interpreters can do their work well, I kindly ask you to pause after I put a question to you before giving your answer, although I don't believe we will have any problems in that regard. We will start with annex 1 to your statement. That's the document that both you and the Honourable Trial Chamber should have before you. In this annex, on page 3 in the B/C/S, that's part of what you entitled, "Introduction," in paragraph 1, you state that units of MUP of SAO Krajina or rather RSK and especially special purpose units of MUP took part in various military operations which the self-declared SAO Krajina conducted in 1991. In connection with this, can you tell us which military operations did the self-declared SAO Krajina carry out in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. When I was writing this report, I was, of course, concentrating on events mentioned in the indictment of Mr. Martic, and those operations or armed actions that are mentioned in his indictment were obvious military operations I'm referring to in the beginning of this report, and as per the documentary evidence, different units of SAO Krajina Police took part in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If I've understood you well, Mr. Kerkkanen, what you had in mind were precisely the allegations contained in the indictment concerning some specific military actions and it was with regard to those actions that you wrote that MUP units of SAO Krajina or the RSK took part in military actions conducted by the self-declared SAO Krajina in 1991. I have another or a further question in relation to this. Did you observe in the indictment that with regard to every single operation alleged in the indictment, when it comes to the period of 1990 and 1991, there is mention of the activities of the so-called Serb forces which includes the JNA, the Territorial Defence, the police of Krajina, the special units of police of Krajina, or however they are termed in the indictment? The question is, on the basis of the documents you reviewed, were you able to arrive at the conclusion that the SAO Krajina conducted military operations in 1991 and that these were in fact operations carried out by the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Well, first, I want to refer to the previous question. I wrote in my report also about fighting that, for example, in Glina, that is not, as far as I remember specifically mentioned in the indictment, in July 1991. Regarding these armed operations or fightings in the area of SAO Krajina especially in 1991, on the basis of documents I reviewed, and I wrote this article, it's very clear that SAO Krajina was very actively participating with its units in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely in relation to 1991, which I believe is quite typical of this, I have the following question: Did you come by any document or piece of information which speaks of the action aimed at deblocking the blocked military garrisons and features throughout the Republic of Croatia including the territory of the SAO Krajina which were conducted or rather which was conducted by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember correctly, I have seen documents that speak about the JNA trying to deblock some military garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Further to your answer to my last question, Mr. Kerkkanen, these military operations you mention in the introduction, were they separate and independent from these actions aimed at deblocking conducted by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. At least some of these operations were independent, and it's well known also on the basis of this documentation I reviewed and I used in this report that they were operations that were carried jointly by the JNA and different SAO Krajina units, police units and Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your cross-examination, we will probably get back to these -- this topic but we will refer to specific actions. So I will not dwell on this matter. Let us look at the second page of your introduction, or rather the page after the introduction, which is entitled, part 1, Milan Martic and SAO, RS Krajina, Ministry of Interior, namely items 1 and 2 -- or rather item 1.2 where you talk about the situation in SAO, RS Krajina, and you state that according to the Statute of the Serbian autonomous district Krajina dated 21 December 1990, the SAO Krajina executed laws, other ordinances and general acts of the Republic of Croatia and the SFRY. In the following sentence, you state that on the 18th of March 1991 the Statute was amended and that wherever the Republic of Croatia and its laws were mentioned, the federal state was now introduced as a result of these amendments. My question is the following: Do you know that the Croatian authorities in February 1991 took a decision to secede from Yugoslavia whereby the federal regulations ceased to be valid in the territory of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Well, I feel that this is not within the scope of my testimony to really answer this question. I'm testifying about these documents and what I wrote on the basis of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I would imagine, Mr. Kerkkanen, that it's a simple question to answer. If you do know, you do say you know. If you don't know, you say you don't know. Independent of what your testimony was, do you know of this decision to secede or don't you know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not familiar with this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milovancevic, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, Mr. Kerkkanen, at the very top of the page, that's a continuation of the text I just read out to you, you state that the powers of the Ministry of Interior in the territory of RSK were abolished on the 19th of January 1991, when a notification or information was issued on the establishment of the Ministry of the Interior of the SAO Krajina. My question is: Is the statement in the paragraph 1.3 correct that on the 19th January 1991 a decree was passed on the internal organisation and work of the Ministry of the Interior of SAO Krajina, or to simplify my question: Was it the case of a decree establishing the Ministry of the Interior of SAO Krajina or the Secretariat of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: No. The Secretariat of the SAO Krajina was already established on the 4th of January 1991. This decree from the 19th of January 1991 is, as its title states, decree on internal organisation and operation of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1.3, you state at the very top, that the decree on the internal organisation of the ministry was issued on the 19th of January 1991. Now my question to it you was it a decree on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior or of the Secretariat of the Interior of the SAO Krajina in relation to this there is the Exhibit 1960 but there is actually another exhibit that you mention, which talks about the Secretariat and not of the ministry. My colleague is on his feet, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt but I thought that perhaps these documents that are being referred to are -- could be called up on e-court for the witness to look at if there are going to be questions about it. Also, we have on the cart here in front of us in hard copy all of the documents that are cited in this report of the witness, and I don't know if it would be of assistance for the witness to have these hard copies available so he could refer even more quickly to documents. I leave that to the Court and to Defence counsel but I just thought I would make them available. It makes it easier for him to flip through them and refer to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting. May I just add this little point, Mr. Milovancevic? I think the witness's report at page 5 states quite clearly that it is the internal organisation and operation of the Ministry of the Interior. If -- no point is being served by asking him whether it is the ministry or the Secretariat. If according to your instructions it was not the ministry but the Secretariat, confront him with the evidence that says it was the Secretariat and let's hear what he's got to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, you state that the executive council of the SAO Krajina took a decision on the 1st of April to unify the SAO Krajina with the Republic of Serbia, whereby it was also decided that the laws and regulations of the Republic of Serbia were to be valid and in force in the entire territory. Here is my question: Do you know that in order for any specific regulation of the Republic of Serbia to apply, it was necessary to pass a special decision to that effect? Therefore, this was a general decision on the unification with the Republic of Serbia on the 1st of April 1991 but do you not know that the executive council was also duty bound to pass a separate decision stating such and such regulations apply to the territory of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt your cross-examination, Mr. Milovancevic. I'm not quite sure I understand either your question or its purpose. The witness has given a report of what he was aware of, that a decision was made to incorporate the SAO Krajina into the Republic of Serbia and apply the laws of Serbia in the territory of the SAO Krajina. And if you want to ask that question that you have asked, I don't see why you asked it in relation to this point. You can just find out if he's aware that specific laws were incorporated specifically each time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was precisely what I wanted to ask the witness. Thank you for your suggestion. Could we please see on our screens Prosecution Exhibit 2034, which is linked with footnote 9? That's the law on the application of the laws and regulations in the territory of the SAO Krajina, dated 5th of June 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document, Mr. Kerkkanen, I would like to put to you that this law dated 5 June 1991, concerning the application of regulations of Serbia in Krajina, provides in Article 1 that these laws of the Republic of Serbia would apply in those areas where there are no RSK regulations existing, and in paragraph 2, that the decision shall be taken by the government of the SAO Krajina or by ministers individually. Therefore, in order for a piece of legislation to apply, a decision to that effect had to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document has come up on my monitor but I'm not sure if it's come up on the court monitors. I don't know if the witness is able to see it or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It has come up on my monitor. I'm not sure whether the witness has it. Mr. Kerkkanen, do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have it and my screen. I would like to go further down. Stop. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: It's possible, rather, if possible, can Article 2 be shown on the monitor of the law on the implementation of regulations of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of the SAO Krajina. In Article 2, it says that the government of the SAO Krajina or the appropriate minister will reissue a decision on each and every case of implementing these regulations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not what my article 2 says. My article 2 says, "Cases in judicial administrative and misdemeanour proceedings, administrative disputes and all other proceedings instigated pursuant to the laws of the Republic of Croatia shall be completed in accordance with such laws."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me, there may be a misunderstanding here. Let me just check whether we have the correct document on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This should be Exhibit 2034 from the Prosecution list, the law on the implementation of regulations of the Republic of Serbia in the territory of the SAO Krajina. Can we scroll up to the beginning of the document, just so we can check it's the right document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document we have on the screen says, "law on the application of regulations of the Republic of Serbia in the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In Article 2 in B/C/S, Your Honours, the text reads in the way I cited to Mr. Kerkkanen. It appears to be mistranslated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then we have a problem, Mr. Milovancevic. We must get the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to settle this matter, I suggest that we return to this document later on, in order not to waste time now. So I will move on and we will return to this question later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The reason I put the previous question to you, sir, was that there is something in paragraph 1.3, the second passage, which says that based on the SAO Krajina executive council decision on the 1st of April 1991, the law on internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia was de facto in force in the SAO Krajina from the beginning of April 1991. I will not ask you what de facto means here. I will, rather, go on to the rest of the sentence, which says, that in addition, or the rest of the passage, in addition on the 2nd of April 1991, a decision was published on the implementation of laws and other regulations on the territory of the SAO Krajina providing that federal regulations and regulations of the SAO Krajina shall be implemented on the SAO Krajina territory. These two sentences seem to contradict each other.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. I have to say that I'm not a lawyer. I'm a researcher and as a researcher I was writing this report and reading these documents that were -- I was paid -- I was basing -- on which I was basing this report. The fact -- de facto in the middle of this paragraph means because on the 1st of April 1991, on the basis of cited document, the laws and constitution of the Republic of Serbia in general were recognised and more specifically it was on the 1st of August 1991, as exhibit number 1044 states that the decision to implement specifically the law and internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia in the territory of the SAO Krajina was taken by the SAO Krajina government. So there is a gap from the 1st of April until the 1st of August 1991, where laws of the Republic of Serbia were valid as far as I understand, on the basis of these documents in the SAO Krajina but specifically the law on internal affairs was accepted on the 1st of August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I just showed you, evidently by mistake, Article 2 of the law on the monitor, whereas I should have put to you paragraph 2 of Article 1, which is on page 1 of the translation, so please let's go back to this document now. Could we see Article 1 of this law, not Article 2 but Article 1? In the second paragraph of this Article, the text reads in the way I quoted to you, Mr. Kerkkanen, that is that the laws and other legal enactments of the Republic of Serbia shall be applied if there were no such regulations passed by the SAO Krajina, and that it would be the government of the SAO Krajina making the decision on this. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see the phrase "if no such enactments" -- I beg your pardon if there were no such regulations passed by the SAO Krajina, in that paragraph. It just says that the laws and legal enactments of the Republic of Serbia shall apply in the Autonomous District of Krajina cited by the government of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina or its individual ministries, where the legal issues concerned fall within the jurisdiction. But it doesn't say if there were no such regulations passed by the SAO Krajina. It is important to quote correctly to the witness, Mr. Milovancevic, so that he doesn't get confused and the record doesn't get confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the first paragraph, excuse me, in the first paragraph of this Article, that is precisely what it says. My question had to do with the witness's statement that the law on the interior was in force from the 1st of April, whereas it was in fact passed in August by a decision of the government as provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 1, which we see on the monitor. That was the point of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then it becomes important, Mr. Milovancevic, to focus the attention of the witness to the correct paragraph. You focused the attention of everybody on the second paragraph of Article 1. That's where we looked at. And we looked at that as the basis for your questions. Now, if your questions relate also to paragraph 1, then focus the witness's attention on the entire Article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so in future, Your Honour. Thank you. I was not sufficiently precise, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, do you know whether this decision passed by the government of the SAO Krajina on the 1st of April 1991 on joining the SAO Krajina to Serbia was accepted by Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 3 or rather the third paragraph on page 5 you say that these rulings effectively meant that the self-declared SAO Krajina unilaterally excluded itself from the Croatian jurisdiction and placed itself under the jurisdiction of the Republic of Serbia and SFRY. With reference to this let me ask you the following: Did Croatia issue a decision on disassociation from Yugoslavia before this decision was made, that is in February 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's been asked this question and he answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to reformulate my question. On the basis of which documents and which evidence does the witness claim that the Krajina unilaterally extracted itself or excluded itself from the Croatian jurisdiction, and on the basis of what the witness considers that it placed itself under the jurisdiction of the SFRY when in fact it never left the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically, we are talking exactly about those documents that are cited on the page 5 and 6 of this report. As it has been discussed already earlier, the document from the 5th of January 1991 states it clearly, that SAO Krajina excludes itself from the jurisdiction of the Republic of Croatia and then these decrees and decisions taken by the SAO Krajina government later in the spring and summer of 1991 refer to SAO Krajina regulations or SFRY laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, page 6, you say that on the 31st of November, it should probably be the 30th of November because the month of November has only 30 days, but that at the end of November 1991, a law on internal affairs of the SAO Krajina was issued or passed and that it was enacted on the 1st of December 1991, and that the law on internal affairs of the SAO Krajina was adopted on the 26th of February 1992. With reference to this legislation, my question is as follows: Did the decisions of the executive council of the SAO Krajina and the decisions of the assembly when passing these laws provide for the Ministry of the Interior of the SAO Krajina becoming or being a constituent part of the ministry in the Yugoslav federation and cooperate with it -- cooperating with it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I should refresh my memory by seeing these documents in front of me. I don't remember by heart all the content of these different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we please see on the monitor document 208 from the Prosecution list? It's the law on internal affairs of the SAO Krajina signed by Mr. Milan Babic, the Prime Minister. Before the document appears on the monitor, we will look at Article 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want us to call Article 30 on the screen or to call the law on the screen, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as the law is now on the monitor, I wish to scroll down to Article 30 of this law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I understand you. If you can scroll down to Article 30 of the law, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It should be page 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Article 30 provides that the Ministry of the Interior shall cooperate with the organs of internal affairs in the federation and in other republics and give them help in executing tasks from their jurisdiction. These relations are provided for by the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The law on internal affairs of the Republic of Serbian Krajina on the 26th of February 1992, Prosecution Exhibit 1943, and footnote 18 on this page, this document refers to command authority. And Article 33 of the law passed in November or Article 42 from the law passed in February are one and the same and provide for employees of the Ministry of the Interior being duty bound to carry out all orders issued by the minister or other superior. That's on page 6 in B/C/S. Apart from orders the implementation of which would constitute a crime. When looking through these documents, and you have mentioned almost 100.000 pages, did you ever come across any orders issued by Mr. Martic ordering the commission of any crime?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't come across with this kind of documents or orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I think this is a convenient time to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Then the Court will adjourn until tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of May, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
